story_type: carrier landing goes wrong: bomber loses its tailhook on touchdown and rolls into the barrier, historic color film
hook: Its tailhook tore off the instant it touched down.
narration: This bomber's tailhook tore away the moment it touched the deck.
It was an AJ Savage, landing on the carrier USS Midway in the early 1950s.
A tailhook snags one of the wires stretched across the deck and drags a landing plane to a stop in a few seconds.
Midway still had a straight deck, so a plane that missed the wires rolled straight toward the jets parked up front.
This Savage had nothing left to catch a wire.
outcome: It rolled into the barrier and damaged a Grumman F9F jet parked at the front of the deck.
title: Tailhook tore off as it hit the deck
description:
Navy color film from USS Midway in the early 1950s shows AJ Savage bombers and F2H Banshee jets at work. One Savage lost its tailhook as it touched down and rolled into the barrier, damaging a parked Grumman F9F.

Footage: U.S. Navy film, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Midway_Flight_Ops_1950.webm
